newsitem.title: USA: Jury awards $23 mln against NYC's HHC.
newsitem.headline: Jury awards $23 mln against NYC's HHC.

text.p: A Manhattan jury has found that New York City Health and Hospitals Corp. should pay $23 million to a 12-year-old girl who received permanent neurological injuries during her delivery and birth, a lawyer in the case said Tuesday.
The Manhattan Supreme Court jury returned its verdict Monday night after a three-week trial, said Thomas Moore, a lawyer representing the girl and her family.
The plaintiffs had alleged that Judy Martelly was permanently injured due to the negligence of the staff at Metropolitan Hospital, where she was born in 1984.
Moore alleged that the hospital missed three opportunities to rescue the girl from danger in a high-risk labor and birth because of lack of experience and supervision of the residents on duty.
Martelly suffers from spastic quadriplegia, is unable to use any of her limbs, and needs complete assistance with all of her daily needs. She is severely retarded and unable to speak.
